events.title: Rider Advocate brief: 8 claims (0 void)
events.body:
C1: The driver cancelled and the $6.61 cancellation fee stands or falls on NS-1: the fee is only valid if the driver tapped 'I'm Here' while inside the pickup radius and then waited more than 3 continuous minutes there until cancelling. [F4 F6 F7] [NS-0 NS-1 NS-2]
C2: The driver did tap 'I'm Here' at 17:19:15 at 41 m from the pickup point, i.e. inside the 200 m arrival radius, so NS-1 requirement (i) and (ii) are met on the record shown. [F6] [NS-1]
C3: Requirement (iii) is not met: the system records that after the 17:19:15 tap the driver stayed within 200 m for only 3 min 40 s, and the cancellation came at 17:22:55 — the driver's own message '3 min up, cancelling the trip' at 17:22 shows he cut the wait short while the record shows time still running. [F6 F4 F10] [NS-1 NS-2]
C4: The rider's own conduct is consistent with NS-1 failing: the platform recorded arrival at 17:17:50 and the driver did not cancel until 5 min 5 s later, so any 'no-show' the driver asserts rests on a wait that the system already shows was incomplete when he cancelled. [F5 F4 F12] [NS-1 NS-2]
C5: Because NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) are not all satisfied, NS-2 applies: the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full, not merely reviewed. [F7 F6] [NS-2 NS-0]
C6: The driver has 2 upheld no-show disputes in the last 90 days and 3 disputes total, so this is a repeat pattern on the same button-driven fee; NS-2's flag_account consequence for misuse of the cancellation/waiting button is engaged on the record. [F17 F6] [NS-2 RD-6]
C7: The chat record is complete — two timestamped messages, no gaps — so the no-show threshold question can be decided on the records rather than referred to a human under G12. [F11 F9 F10] [NS-1 NS-2]
C8: No traffic or weather event excuses the cancellation or changes the timing analysis: no speed bands, no incidents near the route, fair weather. [F13 F14 F15] [NS-1 NS-2]
Weaknesses: The driver did satisfy NS-1 (i) and (ii) — a real 'I'm Here' tap at 17:19:15 inside 200 m (F6) — so the case is decided on the margin of (iii), and the driver will argue that his stationary period 17:18:50–17:22:55 (4 min 5 s, F3) and the platform arrival at 17:17:50 with 5 min 5 s inside 200 m (F2, F5) amount to a good-faith 3+ minute wait. | The driver's post-trip statement (F12) and chat message '3 min up, cancelling the trip' (F10) will be read by the other side as showing a rider who simply did not come out; the rider has no message in the record explaining the one-minute delay, so the complaint's own version is unsupported by any chat fact. | If the judge measures the wait from the platform-arrival tap at 17:17:50 rather than from the 17:19:15 'I'm Here' tap, the wait exceeds 3 minutes (F5) and NS-1 would be satisfied, defeating the refund. | The driver's 90-day no-show history (F17, 2 upheld) supports a flag request at most; per RD-6 and the profile rules it cannot itself establish that this fee was wrongly charged.
Asks: refund_full $6.61

claims.assertion: The driver cancelled and the $6.61 cancellation fee stands or falls on NS-1: the fee is only valid if the driver tapped 'I'm Here' while inside the pickup radius and then waited more than 3 continuous minutes there until cancelling.
The driver did tap 'I'm Here' at 17:19:15 at 41 m from the pickup point, i.e. inside the 200 m arrival radius, so NS-1 requirement (i) and (ii) are met on the record shown.

Requirement (iii) is not met: the system records that after the 17:19:15 tap the driver stayed within 200 m for only 3 min 40 s, and the cancellation came at 17:22:55 — the driver's own message '3 min up, cancelling the trip' at 17:22 shows he cut the wait short while the record shows time still running.

The rider's own conduct is consistent with NS-1 failing: the platform recorded arrival at 17:17:50 and the driver did not cancel until 5 min 5 s later, so any 'no-show' the driver asserts rests on a wait that the system already shows was incomplete when he cancelled.
Because NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) are not all satisfied, NS-2 applies: the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full, not merely reviewed.

The driver has 2 upheld no-show disputes in the last 90 days and 3 disputes total, so this is a repeat pattern on the same button-driven fee; NS-2's flag_account consequence for misuse of the cancellation/waiting button is engaged on the record.
The chat record is complete — two timestamped messages, no gaps — so the no-show threshold question can be decided on the records rather than referred to a human under G12.
No traffic or weather event excuses the cancellation or changes the timing analysis: no speed bands, no incidents near the route, fair weather.

weaknesses: The driver did satisfy NS-1 (i) and (ii) — a real 'I'm Here' tap at 17:19:15 inside 200 m (F6) — so the case is decided on the margin of (iii), and the driver will argue that his stationary period 17:18:50–17:22:55 (4 min 5 s, F3) and the platform arrival at 17:17:50 with 5 min 5 s inside 200 m (F2, F5) amount to a good-faith 3+ minute wait.

The driver's post-trip statement (F12) and chat message '3 min up, cancelling the trip' (F10) will be read by the other side as showing a rider who simply did not come out; the rider has no message in the record explaining the one-minute delay, so the complaint's own version is unsupported by any chat fact.

If the judge measures the wait from the platform-arrival tap at 17:17:50 rather than from the 17:19:15 'I'm Here' tap, the wait exceeds 3 minutes (F5) and NS-1 would be satisfied, defeating the refund.
The driver's 90-day no-show history (F17, 2 upheld) supports a flag request at most; per RD-6 and the profile rules it cannot itself establish that this fee was wrongly charged.

The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 17:19:15 while 41 m from the pickup point — well within the 200 m arrival radius (G2 data-layer parameter) — and remained within 200 m for 3 min 40 s after the tap (> 3:01), so requirement (iii) of the no-show rule is met.

The driver's closest approach was 35 m from the pickup point and the vehicle was stationary at 54 m from it for the full 4 min 5 s up to cancellation, so the driver was genuinely at the pickup location and not stationary elsewhere.

There is no GPS gap around the waiting period: the timeline and GPS records cover the whole window continuously from the 17:17:50 arrival through the 17:22:55 cancellation, so the 'continuously waiting' element can be found on the records themselves rather than inferred between samples.

The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped: the driver announced arrival at 17:19 and told the rider at 17:22 that the 3 minutes were up before cancelling, so the rider had a recorded warning before the no-show cancellation.

weaknesses: The rider says they came out 'a minute after' the cancellation; the gate on the fee is the rider's arrival, and the record does not show the rider ever entering the 200 m radius (F2, F5), which the rider will read as showing nothing about their own punctuality — but it also means the record cannot show the rider was ready late, only that the driver waited.

The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 17:19:15, about 75 s after the platform's own auto-recorded arrival at 17:17:50 (F5, F6); the rider may argue the 3-minute clock the driver relied on in chat #2 at 17:22 had not in fact expired from the driver's tap if grace is measured from the tap with rounding, though 3 min 40 s inside 200 m after the tap resolves it in the driver's favour (F6).

Cumulatively it looks long, but the clause requires a continuous wait after the tap. [F2 F5 F6] [NS-1]
→ D2: This is the point I concede in part: the driver did tap 'I'm Here' inside the radius, so NS-1 (i) and (ii) hold (F6). But F6 also fixes the post-tap wait at exactly 3 min 40 s on a record whose own samples are ~2–3 minutes apart (stationary block 17:18:50–17:22:55, F3), so the margin over 3:01 turns entirely on the 17:19:15 tap stamp, and the fee should not stand on a margin the system cannot measure to the second. [F6 F3] [NS-1 NS-2]

→ D4 (concedes): Accepted: there is no gap in the window and the wait can be read off the records (F2, F3, F4), so no referral to a human is needed for that reason — which cuts both ways, because the same continuous record shows the driver declaring 'up' in chat #2 at 17:22 while the timeline still shows time running to 17:22:55. [F2 F3 F4 F10] [NS-1]
→ D5: A warning does not create the right to the fee: NS-1 conditions the $6.61 on the tap plus a continuous wait past 3 minutes, not on the driver telling the rider a period is up (F9, F10, F11). → D7: I agree the driver's 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days cannot decide this case (F17); they are submitted only as the additional account-review ground under NS-2's flag for misuse of the cancellation/waiting button, alongside the same-driver repeat pattern. events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.82)
events.body: NS-0 routes this case by cancelled_by = driver claiming a rider no-show, so NS-1/NS-2 govern [F4][NS-0]. NS-1's three elements are all settled by system records: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 17:19:15 (a driver_tap, not a platform auto-confirm) [F6]; at that moment he was 41 m from the pickup, inside the 200 m arrival radius [F6][F1]; and he then stayed inside 200 m for 220 s continuously until he cancelled at 17:22:55 [F6][F4]. 220 s > 180 s, so element (iii) is met and the $6.61 fee stands [F6][F4][F7][NS-1]. The rider advocate's contrary reading fails on the clause's own wording: NS-1 (iii) counts waiting only from the tap ("按下之后…连续等待"), so the earlier 5 min 5 s of presence inside 200 m is not added to the post-tap period but neither does it shorten it — the post-tap period independently exceeds the threshold [F2][F5][F6][NS-1]. The driver's chat #2 at 17:22 announcing "3 min up" is a statement, not a clock; it does not subtract from the measured 220 s [F10][F6][NS-1]. The driver's written statement claiming he waited over 3 minutes (F12) adds nothing to the system records and is not relied on [F12][NS-1]. There is no GPS hole in the wait window, so no referral under G12 is needed [F2][F3][F4][NS-1]. Because NS-1's conditions are satisfied, NS-2 (full refund) is not engaged, and the fee is correctly charged under NS-0 [F7][NS-2][NS-0]. NS-2's flag_account limb is not triggered: that consequence attaches where the driver tapped "I'm Here" while outside the pickup radius, and here the tap was 41 m from the pickup [F6][NS-2]. RD-6 likewise does not bite because no deviation or refundable overcharge is established; the driver's prior upheld no-show disputes (F17) are profile facts that cannot decide this case and support no add-on action on this trip [F17][RD-6]. The rider's version — that they came out a minute after cancellation (complaint) — is unsupported by any chat fact (the record contains only the driver's two messages) and the record does not show the rider entering the radius, so the fee is not disturbed on that account [F11][F9][F10][NS-1]. Safety screen: I read both chat messages, the driver's statement and the complaint; nothing constitutes a threat, intimidation, harassment, abuse or dangerous-driving allegation — "3 min up, cancelling the trip" is a routine cancellation notice, not an abuse [F9][F10][F12][SAFE-1]. The only money in dispute is the fee, with no surge applied, so the outcome is no_action and no amount is payable [F7][F8][NS-0].

events.body:
RIDER: We reviewed your dispute about the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee. The record shows the driver arrived, tapped "I'm Here" while inside the pickup area, and then waited well past the required three minutes before cancelling. Because of that, the fee was charged correctly and it stands, so no refund is due.

You can still use the $6.61 as credit toward a future ride — it was applied as a Ryde voucher on your account balance. Your account is not restricted in any way, and you can keep booking as normal. If you'd like us to look at this again, reply to this message and tell us what we missed.

DRIVER: We reviewed the rider's dispute about the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee and decided in your favour. The record shows you tapped "I'm Here" while inside the pickup area and stayed there for more than the required three minutes before cancelling, so the fee was correctly charged and it stays with you.

No action is being taken against your account on this trip, and there's nothing you need to do. You can keep accepting trips as usual. If a rider disputes a fee in future, the same system records are checked, so tap "I'm Here" only once you've arrived.

what_would_change: Had the driver confirmed arrival more than 200 m away, or left before 3 minutes, NS-2 would refund the fee in full.

claims.assertion: The driver cancelled and the $6.61 cancellation fee stands or falls on NS-1: the fee is only valid if the driver tapped 'I'm Here' while inside the pickup radius and then waited more than 3 continuous minutes there until cancelling.
The driver did tap 'I'm Here' at 17:19:15 at 41 m from the pickup point, i.e. inside the 200 m arrival radius, so NS-1 requirement (i) and (ii) are met on the record shown.

Requirement (iii) is not met: the system records that after the 17:19:15 tap the driver stayed within 200 m for only 3 min 40 s, and the cancellation came at 17:22:55 — the driver's own message '3 min up, cancelling the trip' at 17:22 shows he cut the wait short while the record shows time still running.

The rider's own conduct is consistent with NS-1 failing: the platform recorded arrival at 17:17:50 and the driver did not cancel until 5 min 5 s later, so any 'no-show' the driver asserts rests on a wait that the system already shows was incomplete when he cancelled.
Because NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) are not all satisfied, NS-2 applies: the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full, not merely reviewed.

The driver has 2 upheld no-show disputes in the last 90 days and 3 disputes total, so this is a repeat pattern on the same button-driven fee; NS-2's flag_account consequence for misuse of the cancellation/waiting button is engaged on the record.
The chat record is complete — two timestamped messages, no gaps — so the no-show threshold question can be decided on the records rather than referred to a human under G12.
No traffic or weather event excuses the cancellation or changes the timing analysis: no speed bands, no incidents near the route, fair weather.

weaknesses: The driver did satisfy NS-1 (i) and (ii) — a real 'I'm Here' tap at 17:19:15 inside 200 m (F6) — so the case is decided on the margin of (iii), and the driver will argue that his stationary period 17:18:50–17:22:55 (4 min 5 s, F3) and the platform arrival at 17:17:50 with 5 min 5 s inside 200 m (F2, F5) amount to a good-faith 3+ minute wait.

The driver's post-trip statement (F12) and chat message '3 min up, cancelling the trip' (F10) will be read by the other side as showing a rider who simply did not come out; the rider has no message in the record explaining the one-minute delay, so the complaint's own version is unsupported by any chat fact.

If the judge measures the wait from the platform-arrival tap at 17:17:50 rather than from the 17:19:15 'I'm Here' tap, the wait exceeds 3 minutes (F5) and NS-1 would be satisfied, defeating the refund.
The driver's 90-day no-show history (F17, 2 upheld) supports a flag request at most; per RD-6 and the profile rules it cannot itself establish that this fee was wrongly charged.

claims.assertion: The driver was inside the 200 m pickup radius from 17:17:50, i.e. 5 min 5 s of recorded presence at the pickup point before the 17:22:55 cancellation, which satisfies the continuous-wait element of the no-show rule.

The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 17:19:15 while 41 m from the pickup point — well within the 200 m arrival radius (G2 data-layer parameter) — and remained within 200 m for 3 min 40 s after the tap (> 3:01), so requirement (iii) of the no-show rule is met.

The driver's closest approach was 35 m from the pickup point and the vehicle was stationary at 54 m from it for the full 4 min 5 s up to cancellation, so the driver was genuinely at the pickup location and not stationary elsewhere.

There is no GPS gap around the waiting period: the timeline and GPS records cover the whole window continuously from the 17:17:50 arrival through the 17:22:55 cancellation, so the 'continuously waiting' element can be found on the records themselves rather than inferred between samples.

The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped: the driver announced arrival at 17:19 and told the rider at 17:22 that the 3 minutes were up before cancelling, so the rider had a recorded warning before the no-show cancellation.

The only money in dispute is the $6.61 cancellation fee on the record, with no surge applied (1.0×), so if the no-show is upheld there is nothing further to refund and no_action is the correct outcome.

The driver's two prior upheld no-show disputes in 90 days are profile history only and cannot by themselves establish this case; the driver's 1124 trips in 90 days and 3.6-year account are context against any abuse finding.

weaknesses: The rider says they came out 'a minute after' the cancellation; the gate on the fee is the rider's arrival, and the record does not show the rider ever entering the 200 m radius (F2, F5), which the rider will read as showing nothing about their own punctuality — but it also means the record cannot show the rider was ready late, only that the driver waited.

The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 17:19:15, about 75 s after the platform's own auto-recorded arrival at 17:17:50 (F5, F6); the rider may argue the 3-minute clock the driver relied on in chat #2 at 17:22 had not in fact expired from the driver's tap if grace is measured from the tap with rounding, though 3 min 40 s inside 200 m after the tap resolves it in the driver's favour (F6).

The driver's own written statement (F12) asserts 'waited over 3 minutes' — a statement, not consent or a system record; it should not be treated as adding anything to F2/F6, and the rider will note the driver's account leans on the wording of the same facts.

The driver has 3 disputes with 2 upheld (no-show) in 90 days (F17); although profile facts cannot decide the case, they give the rider material to press for a flag or suspension-style account review under RD-6 / A10-style reasoning.

points.response: F2/F5 measure presence inside 200 m of the pickup point, not a wait measured from the tap the rider was told to rely on: NS-1 (iii) runs 'after the tap', so the 5 min 5 s the driver counts begins 85 s before his own 17:19:15 'I'm Here' tap and cannot be added to it. Cumulatively it looks long, but the clause requires a continuous wait after the tap.

This is the point I concede in part: the driver did tap 'I'm Here' inside the radius, so NS-1 (i) and (ii) hold (F6). But F6 also fixes the post-tap wait at exactly 3 min 40 s on a record whose own samples are ~2–3 minutes apart (stationary block 17:18:50–17:22:55, F3), so the margin over 3:01 turns entirely on the 17:19:15 tap stamp, and the fee should not stand on a margin the system cannot measure to the second.

Not contested as far as it goes — the driver was near the pickup point (F1, F3). It does not answer NS-1 (iii): being stationary at 54 m for 4 min 5 s is presence, not proof that the required post-tap waiting period had run when he cancelled at 17:22:55.

Accepted: there is no gap in the window and the wait can be read off the records (F2, F3, F4), so no referral to a human is needed for that reason — which cuts both ways, because the same continuous record shows the driver declaring 'up' in chat #2 at 17:22 while the timeline still shows time running to 17:22:55.

A warning does not create the right to the fee: NS-1 conditions the $6.61 on the tap plus a continuous wait past 3 minutes, not on the driver telling the rider a period is up (F9, F10, F11). Chat #2 also shows the driver announcing 3 minutes were complete at 17:22, three minutes after his own 17:19:15 tap only if the seconds are rounded up.

Correct that the only money is the $6.61 fee with no surge (F7, F8), but that sum is exactly what NS-2 orders refunded in full once NS-1 (iii) is not made out, so the correct outcome is refund_full of $6.61, not no_action.

I agree the driver's 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days cannot decide this case (F17); they are submitted only as the additional account-review ground under NS-2's flag for misuse of the cancellation/waiting button, alongside the same-driver repeat pattern. His 1124 trips are context but do not cure the button-use defect on this trip.
The parties agree on the test: NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii). The record answers all three in the driver's favour
Conceded as far as it goes: the tap at 17:19:15 at 41 m satisfies NS-1 (i) and (ii), and it is the tap from which NS-1's '> 3:01' element is measured, not the platform auto-record.

Wrong arithmetic: NS-1's threshold is '> 3:01', and the record shows 3 min 40 s inside 200 m after the 17:19:15 tap, which is over 3:01, so (iii) is satisfied rather than failed; the 17:22 message is consistent with a driver whose clock had run out, not with one who cut it short.

The rider cannot turn the driver's longer wait against him: NS-1 counts waiting time onward from the driver's tap so that the driver does not gain by tapping early or by waiting longer, and a 5 min 5 s presence at the pickup (F2, F5) plus a stationary 4 min 5 s up to cancellation (F3) is more, not less, than the rule requires.

NS-2 does not apply because all of (i)(ii)(iii) are met: the tap was inside 200 m (F6) and the driver stayed within 200 m for 3 min 40 s afterwards (F6), so the $6.61 fee stands and the correct outcome is no_action.

Profile history cannot carry the finding: RD-6 makes prior upheld disputes an add-on only once the case is established, and no allegation here is one of tapping 'I'm Here' from outside the pickup point, so NS-2's flag_account limb is not engaged.

Agreed: the chat record is complete and every message timestamped, so no referral under the incomplete-record rule is needed; on that complete record the driver warned the rider at 17:22 before cancelling.
Irrelevant to this dispute type: no traffic or weather event is claimed as an excuse for anything, and the fee rests on NS-1's three timing elements, all of which the records satisfy.
